The sizes don't scale consistently. 32 and 48 are tall with a prominent mast, but 16–24 are squashed flat. The mast disappears at 16 and is only a stub at 20/24.
At 16px the hull and cabin merge into a tiny two-tier shape, a small tub with a box on it. There is no cargo or ship cue left.

Solid: the container stack becomes one plain slab with no knockouts. The container divisions that carry the 'cargo' meaning in the outline are lost at every size, and the solid reads as a generic boat or barge.
Solid 16px is a tiny trapezoid with a dash above it. It can't be recognised and looks clogged next to the solid truck and train.
Recognition depends on the hull trapezoid alone. The 'cargo' part (stacked containers) is too small relative to the hull to read as containers, especially below 32px.
There's no waterline or bow cue, so the hull could be a bowl, basket or tray.
fixes: Redraw 16/20/24 so the ship fills the frame like its neighbours: the hull should span about 20 of 24 units wide, and the whole ship about 16–18 units tall, matching the visual weight of the truck and train.

Make the container stack taller and more prominent: two tiers or at least three clearly separated container blocks that take up about 40% of the height. Draw them separately at each size with whole-pixel gaps so the divisions survive at 16px. Use two blocks at 16px if needed.
Give the hull a ship profile: a raised or angled bow on one side and a flatter stern, not a symmetric tray. Optionally add a short bridge/superstructure at the stern instead of a thin mast.
Keep one structural cue (bridge or mast) at every size, including 16px, at the same relative proportion, so the 16–48 drawings read as one design.

Solid: knock out the gaps between containers (at least 1px at 16/20) so the containers stay visible. Consider a knocked-out deck line between the containers and the hull. Keep the outer footprint identical to the outline.
Optionally add a simple wave or waterline under the hull, as the airlines icon uses a runway line, to anchor it as a vessel. Check that it stays open at 16px.

name: Rail

scores.reads_as: At 24–48px: front view of a metro/train car (window, two headlights, splayed rails). At 16px: a rounded box split by one horizontal line on two short legs. It reads as a seat, a barrel or a storage bin, not a train.
problems: The 16px outline drops the window rectangle and both headlight dots. All that's left is a capsule with one horizontal divider line, which is not recognisable as a train. Next to it on the sheet it looks like furniture/armchair, energy (barrel) or a bin.
The 16px solid is a filled rounded block with a single dash knockout. It is almost the same as the cmbs solid and the energy solid on sheet-16, so it is not distinct at the most-used size.
The windscreen and lights carry the train idea at 24px and up, so the 16px drawing does not match the larger sizes.

The footprint is narrow and portrait. At 16px it sits visibly smaller in its box than transportation, marine-shipping and postal-courier, and its width is only about 55–60% of the frame at every size.
At 20–24px the two headlight dots are tiny and close to the window. In the solid version the dot knockouts are barely visible at 20px.
The leg/rail strokes at 16px are very short, so they read as stool legs rather than diverging rails.
fixes: Redraw 16px from the 24px master's structure. Keep a clear window rectangle (stroke outline; solid knockout at least 2px tall and 5–6px wide) and remove the single horizontal divider line.
At 16px keep at least the window plus the lower body edge. If the headlights can't be drawn at least 1.5px with 1px clearance, drop them, but don't replace the window with a line.

Widen the body by about 1–2px at each size (24px: body around 14–15px wide instead of about 12) and lengthen the splayed rail legs so they reach the bottom of the live area. That fills the frame like the siblings and makes the rails read as track.
At 20 and 24px, make the solid headlight knockouts bigger (about 2px diameter) and add more space between them and the window.
As an option, add a short horizontal sleeper/track line under the splayed legs at 16 and 20px to push the reading towards rail and away from furniture or a bin.
After redrawing, compare the 16px solid against cmbs, energy and furniture on sheet-16 to confirm it is distinct.
